conventions: Formatter is Prettier 2.6 via @excalidraw/prettier-config: double quotes, trailing commas, 80-column lines; ESLint runs with --max-warnings=0 and enforces import/order (groups separated by blank lines, type-only imports last).

Cross-package imports use the aliases @excalidraw/common, @excalidraw/element, @excalidraw/element/types and @excalidraw/math; imports inside one package are relative (./arrowheads, ../components/RadioSelection).
Type-only imports use a separate `import type { ... }` statement (consistent-type-imports with separate-type-imports); never mix types into a value import.
Element-package code is plain exported arrow functions with explicit return types and switch over string-literal unions; no classes for new helpers.
Elements are immutable: actions update with newElementWith(el, partial) (bumps version/versionNonce, which history and collaboration rely on); never assign to an element field.
Follow AGENTS.md: use Merge<> from @excalidraw/common/utility-types instead of Omit<> & ..., and app.ownerDocument / app.ownerWindow instead of document / window in new non-test DOM code.
Geometry and render code runs per frame: the default path (no arrowheadSize key) must take no new allocations and must produce byte-identical numbers to today (multiply/divide by exactly 1).
User-facing strings go through t("labels.<key>") from ../i18n; only packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json gets new keys, never another locale.

Tests use vitest globals (describe/it/expect/beforeEach without import); editor tests render <Excalidraw /> with render() from tests/test-utils and drive it through API, UI and Keyboard from tests/helpers, querying controls by data-testid.
Element-package tests import editor test helpers as @excalidraw/excalidraw/tests/helpers/api and the code under test relatively from ../src/<module>.

Names fixed by this change: element property `arrowheadSize`, type `ArrowheadSize`, appState key `currentItemArrowheadSize`, action `actionChangeArrowheadSize` named "changeArrowheadSize", constants ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALES and DEFAULT_ARROWHEAD_SIZE, helpers isArrowheadSize / normalizeArrowheadSize / getArrowheadSizeScale.

decisions.choice: A closed set of named presets "small" | "medium" | "large" mapped by ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALES = { small: 0.5, medium: 1, large: 1.5 } in @excalidraw/common; "medium" is the default (scale 1, today's geometry) and is never stored on an element: an absent key means default.
rejected: numeric scale values on the element
decisions.reason: A closed union restores and validates trivially, maps to RadioSelection like stroke width, and the absent-key default keeps every existing element and snapshot unchanged.

decisions.choice: Only inside getArrowheadPoints in bounds.ts: size = getArrowheadSize(arrowhead) * getArrowheadSizeScale(element.arrowheadSize), after which the existing short-segment fitting (length multiplier and getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment) runs unchanged with that size as the full size; getArrowheadSize(arrowhead) keeps its signature and per-type values.
rejected: adding a size parameter to getArrowheadSize
decisions.reason: getArrowheadPoints is the single function canvas, SVG export, shape cache and bounds all read (NFR-3); for sizes at or below default this equals the smaller of the chosen size and today's auto-shrunk size, and elbowArrow.ts/transform.ts keep reading the unscaled per-type size.

decisions.choice: getArrowheadPoints passes minSize / scale to getArrowheadAngle, so a chosen size draws the same shape as the default at full size and the existing widening still applies when the fitting shrinks the head.
rejected: passing the absolute minSize (small heads would open wider than default)
decisions.reason: FR-2 asks for proportional scaling; dividing by exactly 1 keeps the default byte-identical.

decisions.choice: Linear bounds (getLinearElementRotatedBounds) are extended by the arrowhead extents only for arrow elements whose getArrowheadSizeScale is greater than 1; default and small heads keep today's curve-only bounds.
rejected: always including heads in bounds (changes every existing arrow's bounds and export size, breaking NFR-1)
including heads whenever the key is present (choosing small would grow the bounds)
decisions.reason: Today heads never define the extent; this keeps default bounds identical (AC-2), makes an enlarged head grow the bounds that export sizing, culling and the hit-test prefilter use (AC-3), and never lets a smaller choice grow them.

decisions.choice: Hit-testing follows the scaled head through getElementBounds (the hitElementItself prefilter); the precise test stays against the arrow path as today.
rejected: editing collision.ts / utils.ts to hit-test head outlines
decisions.reason: collision.ts and utils.ts are outside the Gate 0 allowlist and heads are not hit targets today; the head tip sits on the path end so clicks on the head near the tip still hit.

decisions.choice: Elbow routing does not read the size and actionChangeArrowheadSize does not re-route; renderElement.ts, shape.ts and staticSvgScene.ts are not edited.
rejected: re-routing elbow arrows on size change
decisions.reason: Routing reserves space per head type; the 40px arrow canvas padding exceeds the largest lateral head extent at scale 1.5 (bar: 22.5px); shapes already come from getArrowheadPoints.

decisions.choice: Setting the default size writes { arrowheadSize: undefined } via newElementWith (serializes as absent); actionChangeArrowheadSize and paste-styles skip an element whose normalized size already equals the target, so untouched elements gain no key.
rejected: rebuilding element objects without the key in actions
decisions.reason: newElementWith cannot delete keys; skipping no-op elements keeps existing element snapshots (e.g. paste-styles tests) free of a new key.

decisions.choice: restoreElement keeps a valid non-default arrowheadSize on line and arrow elements, deletes the key when the value is invalid or "medium", and leaves an element without the key untouched; restoreAppState falls back to DEFAULT_ARROWHEAD_SIZE for a missing or invalid currentItemArrowheadSize.
decisions.reason: Canonical absence of the default keeps restored scenes byte-identical to today and makes invalid imports render at the default.

decisions.choice: getArrowheadSizeScale returns 1 for any value that is not a key of ARROWHEAD_SIZE_SCALES (including undefined).
decisions.reason: An element received over collaboration from a newer client renders at default instead of NaN geometry (NFR-2).

decisions.choice: actionChangeArrowheadSize renders <fieldset><legend>{t("labels.arrowheadSize")}</legend> with a RadioSelection<ArrowheadSize> (group "arrowhead-size", testIds arrowheadSize-small / arrowheadSize-medium / arrowheadSize-large) reusing FontSizeSmallIcon, FontSizeMediumIcon and FontSizeLargeIcon; it renders right after changeArrowhead in the full panel under predicates.arrowheads and inside actionChangeArrowProperties for the compact and mobile panels.
decisions.reason: Follows the actionChangeStrokeWidth pattern and the existing arrowhead visibility exactly (open question 2 default).

decisions.choice: currentItemArrowheadSize is stored like currentItemEndArrowhead: { browser: true, export: false, server: false }.
decisions.reason: It is a per-user drawing default, not scene data.

decisions.topic: Which new elements take the default
decisions.choice: Arrows created by the drawing tool (App.tsx), flowchart (flowchart.ts), autoshape recognition (convertToShape.ts, App.drawshape.ts) and conversion to sharp or curved arrows (ConvertElementTypePopup.tsx) pass arrowheadSize: <appState>.currentItemArrowheadSize; elbow conversion keeps the element's own size via the existing spread; lines get no size from appState because they draw no heads.
decisions.reason: Mirrors exactly where currentItemStartArrowhead / currentItemEndArrowhead are applied today.

decisions.choice: After all source and test units, a tooling step runs vitest with --update over packages/ only; the only expected snapshot change is the new currentItemArrowheadSize key in appState-capturing snapshots (and the new control in panel DOM snapshots).
decisions.reason: getDefaultAppState gains a key (FR-7), which Gate 0 allows in appState snapshots; reviewers check the diff shows no element or geometry change.

units.behaviour: Scales arrowhead geometry by the element's size inside getArrowheadPoints and extends linear bounds by enlarged arrowheads.
rules: 1. In getArrowheadPoints: `const scale = getArrowheadSizeScale(element.arrowheadSize);` and `const size = getArrowheadSize(arrowhead) * scale;`; the length multiplier, minSize and getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment logic below stay exactly as they are (the fitting runs with the scaled size as the full size).
2. In getArrowheadPoints the angle line becomes `getArrowheadAngle(arrowhead, minSize / scale)`; nothing else in the function changes, so scale 1 yields byte-identical points.
3. getArrowheadSize, getArrowheadAngle, getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment and getCardinalityMarkerScale keep their signatures and bodies.

4. New private `extendBoundsByArrowheads(element: ExcalidrawLinearElement, curve: Drawable, bounds: Bounds, transformXY: (p: GlobalPoint) => GlobalPoint): Bounds`, placed right before getLinearElementRotatedBounds.
5. It returns `bounds` itself (no copy, no allocation) unless isArrowElement(element) and getArrowheadSizeScale(element.arrowheadSize) > 1.

6. Otherwise start min/max from bounds and, for position "start" with element.startArrowhead and "end" with element.endArrowhead (skip a null head), enumerate the head's parts exactly as shape.ts getArrowheadShapes does: circle and circle_outline -> one circle part (the head, offset 0, diameter scale 1); cardinality_one_or_many -> "cardinality_many" offset 0 and "cardinality_one" offset CARDINALITY_ONE_OR_MANY_BAR_OFFSET; cardinality_exactly_one -> "cardinality_one" offset CARDINALITY_INNER_BAR_OFFSET and "cardinality_one" offset 0; cardinality_zero_or_one -> circle part "circle_outline" offset CARDINALITY_ZERO_CIRCLE_OFFSET diameter scale CARDINALITY_ZERO_CIRCLE_SCALE and "cardinality_one" offset CARDINALITY_INNER_BAR_OFFSET; cardinality_zero_or_many -> "cardinality_many" offset 0 and circle part "circle_outline" offset CARDINALITY_ZERO_CIRCLE_OFFSET diameter scale CARDINALITY_ZERO_CIRCLE_SCALE; every other head -> the head itself, offset 0.
7. Each part calls getArrowheadPoints(element, [curve], position, partArrowhead, offset) and skips a null result.
8. A circle part's result is [x, y, diameter]: transform pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(x, y) with transformXY and extend min/max by diameter * diameterScale / 2 on every side.
9. Any other part's result is a flat x, y list: transform each consecutive pair with transformXY and extend min/max; return [minX, minY, maxX, maxY].
10. In getLinearElementRotatedBounds, `coords` starts from extendBoundsByArrowheads(element, shape, [res[0], res[1], res[2], res[3]], transformXY); the bound-text branch after it is unchanged.

rules: 1. `beforeEach(async () => { await render(<Excalidraw />); })` with Excalidraw from "../index" and render from "./test-utils"; read state through window.h (`const { h } = window;`).

2. Arrows come from API.createElement({ type: "arrow", points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(200, 0)], roughness: 0, endArrowhead: "arrow" }); a size is given by spreading `{ ...arrow, arrowheadSize }`; put them in the scene with API.setElements and select with API.setSelectedElements.
3. Click the control with UI.clickOnTestId("arrowheadSize-small" | "arrowheadSize-medium" | "arrowheadSize-large"); read the element back with API.getElement(arrow); undo with Keyboard.undo().
4. Restore with restoreElements(elements, null) and restoreAppState(appState, null) from "../data/restore"; cast invalid inputs with `as any` only at the call site.

5. Export with exportScene({ type: "svg", data: { elements, appState: { viewBackgroundColor: "#ffffff" }, files: {} }, config: { canvasBackgroundColor: false } }) from "../scene/export"; measure a head as the largest |y| over all number pairs parsed from every <path> d attribute (the shaft lies on local y = 0).
6. Copy and paste styles with API.executeAction(actionCopyStyles) / API.executeAction(actionPasteStyles) from "../actions" after selecting the source, then the target.

style_from.reason: Editor test scaffolding: render(<Excalidraw />), API, UI and data-testid queries.

uses.reason: How exportScene is imported and called for SVG.

tests.name: sets the size of the selected arrow and the default
tests.given: one selected default arrow, then a click on arrowheadSize-small
tests.expect: the arrow's arrowheadSize is "small" and h.state.currentItemArrowheadSize is "small"

tests.name: undo restores the previous size
tests.given: the arrow after choosing small, then Keyboard.undo()
tests.expect: the arrow has arrowheadSize undefined (default) again

tests.name: choosing medium clears the size
tests.given: a selected arrow with arrowheadSize "large", then a click on arrowheadSize-medium
tests.expect: arrowheadSize is undefined, JSON.stringify of the element has no arrowheadSize, currentItemArrowheadSize is "medium"

tests.name: new arrows take the chosen size
tests.given: API.setAppState({ currentItemArrowheadSize: "large" }), then UI.createElement("arrow", { x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 0 })

tests.name: paste styles carries the size
tests.given: styles copied from a small arrow and pasted onto a default arrow

tests.name: exports a smaller head to SVG
tests.given: restoreElements of a two-point arrow with arrowheadSize "small" and of the same arrow without it, each exported to SVG
tests.expect: the small arrow's largest path |y| is smaller than the default arrow's

tests.name: restores an arrow without a size unchanged
tests.expect: the restored arrow has no own arrowheadSize key and the same points and endArrowhead

tests.name: restore drops invalid and default sizes
tests.given: restoreElements of arrows with arrowheadSize "huge", "medium" and "small"
tests.expect: the first two have no own arrowheadSize key; the third keeps "small"

tests.name: appState restore defaults the size
tests.given: restoreAppState({}, null), restoreAppState({ currentItemArrowheadSize: "huge" } as any, null) and restoreAppState({ currentItemArrowheadSize: "large" }, null)

rules: 1. New section `### Arrowhead size (2026-11-09) [#6712](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/6712)` followed by a blank line and three bullets, then a blank line.

2. Bullet: linear elements gain optional `arrowheadSize` (`"small" | "medium" | "large"`, type `ArrowheadSize`) scaling both arrowheads; absent means `"medium"`, today's size, so existing scenes render, export and hit-test as before; invalid values restore to the default.

3. Bullet: new `appState.currentItemArrowheadSize` (default `"medium"`, persisted in browser storage only) applied to newly created arrows, and a properties-panel control (action `changeArrowheadSize`) next to the arrowhead pickers; copy/paste styles carries the size.
4. Bullet: `convertToExcalidrawElements` passes `arrowheadSize` through; arrows larger than default include their heads in their bounds.
